rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil reads the disjointed letters as praise of God: He suffices for creation, guides His servants, knows His creatures, and speaks truthfully; yāʾ comes from al-Hādī.
rows.anchor: كافيا لخلقه، هاديا لعباده، الياء من الهادي، عالم ببريته، صادق في قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of Zakariya is a mention of the Lord's blessing; Zakariya is identified as son of Barkhiya.
rows.anchor: يعني نعمة ربك يا محمد، { عبده زكريآ } [آية: 2] ابن برخيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya prayed secretly so people would not remark that an old man was asking for a child in old age.
rows.anchor: لئلا يقول الناس: انظروا إلى هذا الشيخ الكبير، يسأل الولد على كبره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya's bones had weakened and his head had turned white with age.
rows.anchor: يعني ضعف العظم منى، { واشتعل الرأس شيبا } ، يعني بياضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He recalls that he was never disappointed when praying to God and asks not to be disappointed in his prayer for a child now.
rows.anchor: يعني خائبا فيما خلا، كنت تستجيب لي، فلا تخيبني في دعائي إياك بالولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mawālī are the agnatic relatives who would inherit Zakariya's property after his death; his wife was barren, so he asked for a child from God.
rows.anchor: يقول: خفت الكلالة، وهم العصبة من بعد موتي أن يرثوا مالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks that his son inherit his property and the teaching and leadership among the priests of Jacob's family; Jacob and Mary's grandfather Mathan's son Imran were brothers.
rows.anchor: يرث مالي، { ويرث من آل يعقوب } ابن ماثان علمهم، ورياستهم في الأحبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks that the child be righteous.
rows.anchor: { واجعله رب رضيا } [آية: 6]، يعني صالحا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Zakariya's prayer; Gabriel brought the news while Zakariya was praying, and no one before had been named Yahya.
rows.anchor: فأتاه جبريل وهو يصلي، فقال: { يزكريآ إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was so named because God brought him to life through an elderly man and a barren old woman.
rows.anchor: وإنما سماه يحيى؛ لأنه أحياه من بين شيخ كبير وعجوز عاقر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks how he can have a boy when his wife cannot bear children; ʿatiyyan means hardship, and Zakariya was then seventy-five.
rows.anchor: يعني بؤسا، وكان زكريا يومئذ ابن خمس وسبعين سنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel says that this is what Zakariya's Lord has declared: a boy will be born; it is easy for God, who created Zakariya when he was nothing.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا، { قال ربك } إنه ليكون لك غلام، { هو علي هين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya asks for a sign of conception after Gabriel's direct announcement; after conceiving, he will be unable to speak to people for three nights while otherwise sound, as a consequence of asking for a sign.
rows.anchor: يعني علما للحبل، فسأل الآية بعد مشافهة جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speechlessness was not illness or muteness, and God did not prevent Zakariya from remembering Him or praying.
rows.anchor: فإنك تصبح تلك الليلة لا تستنكر من نفسك خرسا، ولا مرضا، ولكن لا تستطيع الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakariya left the mosque's prayer niche for the Children of Israel and wrote them a message with his hand to pray morning and evening.
rows.anchor: يعني من المسجد، { فأوحى إليهم أن سبحوا بكرة وعشيا } [آية: 11]، يقول: كتب كتابا بيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book given to Yahya is the Torah, and taking it firmly means applying oneself to it diligently and consistently.
rows.anchor: يعني التوراة، { بقوة } ، يعني بجد ومواظبة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was given knowledge and understanding as a three-year-old child.
rows.anchor: يعني وأعطينا يحيى العلم والفهم وهو ابن ثلاث سنين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanan means mercy from God; zakāh means that God made Yahya righteous and purified him of sins, and taqī means Muslim.
rows.anchor: يقول: رحمة من عندنا، { وزكاة } ، يعني جعله صالحا وطهره من الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahya was obedient to his parents, not proud of worshipping God, and not disobedient to his Lord.
rows.anchor: يقول: وجعلناه مطيعا لوالديه، { ولم يكن جبارا } ، يعني متكبرا عن عبادة الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's peace on Yahya at birth, death, and resurrection refers to those times; yawm can mean 'when,' as in the creation and resurrection passages cited here.
rows.anchor: يعني على يحيى، عليه السلام، { يوم ولد } ، يعني حين ولد، مثل قوله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary is daughter of Imran son of Mathan; Jacob son of Mathan was his brother, and Mary descended from Solomon son of David.
rows.anchor: يعني في القرآن ابنة عمران بن ماثان، ويعقوب بن ماثان، من نسل سليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew from her family to the eastern quarter because it was winter.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا انفردت، { من أهلها مكانا شرقيا } [آية: 16]، فجلست في المشرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary put a mountain between herself and her family so they could not see her; hijāb likewise means the mountain that hides the sun, a year's journey from Mount Qaf.
rows.anchor: يعني جبلا، فجعلت الجبل بينها وبينهم، فلم يرها أحد منهم، كقوله في ص:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Spirit was Gabriel, who appeared as a well-formed human, a smooth-faced young man with curly hair.
rows.anchor: يعني إنسانا سويا، يعني سوى الخلق، على صور شاب أمرد، جعد الرأس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary took the apparition for a human and called on God for protection, addressing him as God-fearing if he was devoted to God.
rows.anchor: فلما رأته حسبته إنسانا، { قالت إني أعوذ بالرحمن منك إن كنت تقيا } [آية: 18]، يعني مخلصا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel says he is the Lord's messenger, sent by God's command to grant Mary a pure, righteous boy.
rows.anchor: بأمر الله عز وجل، { غلاما زكيا } [آية: 19]، يعني مخلصا، يقول صالحا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary says no man has touched her, meaning she has had no husband, and she has not been a prostitute or committed sexual immorality.
rows.anchor: يعني ولم يكن لي زوج، { ولم أك بغيا } [آية: 20]، يعني ولم أركب فاحشة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel confirms that God will give her a child without a husband; creating a child in her womb without a human father is easy for God.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا، { قال ربك } إنه يكون لك ولد من غير زوج، { هو علي } ، على الله، { هين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus will be a sign for the Children of Israel and a mercy and blessing for those who follow his religion, as in the statement about Muhammad's mission.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولكي نجعله عبرة، { للناس } ، يعني في بني إسرائيل، { ورحمة } ، يعني ونعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' birth without a human father was decreed in the Preserved Tablet and must occur.
rows.anchor: قد قضى الله عز وجل في اللوح المحفوظ أنه كائن لا بد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary was thirteen, bore Jesus in one hour, and he was formed and nursed in an hour at noon; she had menstruated twice before conceiving, lived with him thirty-three years, then six years after his ascension, and died aged fifty-two.
rows.anchor: وهي ابنة ثلاث عشرة سنة، ومكثت مع عيسى، عليه السلام، ثلاثا وثلاثين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary conceived, Jesus was formed, and she nursed him each within an hour at noon, after two menstrual periods.
rows.anchor: فحملته أمه في ساعة واحدة، وصور في ساعة واحدة، وأرضعته في ساعة حين زالت الشمس من يومها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary withdrew with Jesus to a distant place, away from her family beyond the hills.
rows.anchor: يعني فانفردت بعيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم، { مكانا قصيا } [آية: 22]، يعني نائيا من أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labor drove Mary to the palm trunk, which had no fronds; she wished she had died before the living child out of shame before people.
rows.anchor: يعني فألجأها، ولم يكن لها سعف، { قالت } مريم: { يليتني مت قبل هذا } ، الولد حياء من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasyan mansi means something perished and forgotten so that it is no longer remembered.
rows.anchor: يعني كالشيء الهالك الذي لا يذكر فينسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel called from below, on the ground while Mary stood above him on a rise, telling her not to grieve after she wished for death; sariy means a small stream.
rows.anchor: فناداها } جبريل، عليه السلام، { من تحتهآ } ، يعني من أسفل منها في الأرض، وهي فوقه على رابية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sariy means a small river or stream.
rows.anchor: يعني الجدول الصغير من الأنهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janiyyan describes ripe dates; the dry palm turned green before Mary's eyes, and God sent a stream from Jordan to her so she would believe in Jesus and not marvel at him.
rows.anchor: يعني بالجني ما ترطب به من البسر، وكانت شجرة يابسة، فاخضرت وهي تنظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the signs to strengthen Mary's belief in Jesus and keep her from marveling at his birth.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل الله عز وجل ذلك لتؤمن بأمر عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا تعجب منه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the fast Mary vowed as silence; Muqatil reports this through Ikrima, with the chain ending at Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، في قوله: { إني نذرت للرحمن صوما } ، يعني صمتا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary eats dates, drinks sweet water, and rejoices in her child; the fast she vowed means silence, so she is not to speak to anyone about Jesus that day.
rows.anchor: من النخلة، { واشربي } من الماء العذب، { وقري عينا } بالولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary brought Jesus to the Children of Israel in her arms, wrapped in rags; farri means a reprehensible thing.
rows.anchor: إلى بنى إسرائيل في حجرها ملفوفا في خرق، { قالوا يمريم لقد جئت شيئا فريا } [آية: 27]، يقول: أتيت أمرا منكرا.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to explain that they meant Aaron, Moses' brother, because Mary was among his descendants.
rows.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:
" إنما عنوا هارون أخا موسى؛ لأنها كانت من نسله "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Mary's father no man of evil means he was not a fornicator; Imran was a leading Israelite. Her mother was not a prostitute, prompting the question of where the child came from.
rows.anchor:
يعني بزان، كقوله سبحانه:
من أراد بأهلك سوءا
[يوسف: 25]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary pointed to Jesus for them to speak to him; they ask how to address a baby in his mother's lap, wrapped in rags. Zechariah approached and challenged the child to speak in his defense.
rows.anchor: يعني إلى ابنها عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم أن كلموه، { قالوا } ، قال قومها: { كيف نكلم من كان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was a baby in his mother's lap, wrapped in rags; Zechariah asked him to speak up in his defense if he had one.
rows.anchor: فدنا زكريا من الصبي، فقال: تكلم يا صبى بعذرك إن كان لك عذر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' first words were that he is God's servant, directly contradicting Christian claims about him; he says God gave and taught him the Gospel and made him a prophet.
rows.anchor: ف { قال } الصبى، وهو يومئذ ولد، { إني عبد الله } ، وكذبت النصارى فيما يقولون، فأول ما تكلم به الصبي أنه أقر لله بالعبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book given to Jesus is the Gospel, which God taught him.
rows.anchor: يعني أعطاني الإنجيل فعلمنيه، { وجعلني نبيا } [آية: 30]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is a teacher and guide in goodness wherever he is on earth, and God charged him with prayer and almsgiving for life.
rows.anchor: يعني معلما مؤدبا في الخير، { أين ما كنت } من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was charged to obey his mother Mary; he was not arrogant about worship and was not disobedient to God.
rows.anchor: يقول: وأوصاني أن أكون برا بوالدتي، يعني مطيعا لأمي مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Jesus said he was dutiful to his mother but named no father, Zechariah embraced him and testified that he was God's servant and messenger.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكر الوالدة، ولم يذكر الوالد، ضمه زكريا إلى صدره، وقال: أشهد أنك عبد الله ورسوله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' greeting of peace at birth, death, and resurrection refers to those times, including his being raised alive after death in the Hereafter; he then stopped speaking and grew like other children.
rows.anchor: يعني حين ولدت، { ويوم أموت } ، يعني وحين أموت، { ويوم أبعث حيا } [آية: 33]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus son of Mary is the true and just statement about whom the Christians dispute and doubt.
rows.anchor: يعني هذا عيسى ابن مريم قول العدل، يعني الصدق، { الذي فيه يمترون } [آية: 34]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot take a son; He is exalted above that, and when He decrees Jesus in His knowledge He creates by saying 'Be' once, without repeating the utterance.
rows.anchor: يعني عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم، { سبحانه } ، نزه نفسه عز وجل، { إذا قضى أمرا } كان في علمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says 'Be, and it is' is expressed in Persian and that God need not repeat the statement: once He says it, it is.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، أنه قال: { كن فيكون } بالفارسية، لا يثني القول مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus tells the Children of Israel that God is his and their Lord, so they must worship and affirm His oneness; Islam is the straight path and other religions are crooked.
rows.anchor: يعني فوحدوه، { هذا } التوحيد، { صراط مستقيم } [آية: 36]، يعني دين الإسلام مستقيم

rows.speaker: النسطورية
rows.claim: The Nestorians say Jesus is the son of God.
rows.anchor: تحزبوا في عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث فرق: النسطورية

rows.speaker: المار يعقوبية
rows.claim: The Jacobites say Jesus is God.
rows.anchor: والمار يعقوبية قالوا: عيسى هو الله،

rows.speaker: الملكانيون
rows.claim: The Melkites say God is the third of three.
rows.anchor:
إن الله ثالث ثلاثة
[المائدة: 73]، يقول الله: وحده لا شريك له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil affirms that God alone has no partner; those who split into sects over Jesus face woe at the great scene of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: يقول الله: وحده لا شريك له: { فويل للذين كفروا } ، يعني تحزبوا في عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection people will hear and see the warning and other matters most acutely, as in their plea to return and act righteously; today's polytheists are plainly deluded and cannot perceive the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يقول: هم يوم القيامة أسمع قوم وأبصر بما كانوا فيه من الوعيد وغيره، { يوم يأتوننا } في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Regret is when death is made into a white ram and slaughtered between Paradise and Hell while both groups watch; each is told it will remain forever, and the damned would die of regret if God had not decreed their souls remain in their bodies.
rows.anchor: يوم يذبح الموت كأنه كبش أملح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Gabriel slaughters death as a white ram between Paradise and Hell, then announces everlasting life in each abode; the people of Hell would die of regret were their souls not decreed to endure in their bodies.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس، أنه قال: يجعل الموت في صورة كبش أملح، فيذبحه جبريل بين الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When judgment and punishment are settled, disbelievers today are heedless and do not believe what will happen in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا قضي العذاب، { وهم في غفلة } اليوم { وهم لا يؤمنون } [آية: 39]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will make everyone die and remain after them; He inherits the inhabitants of heaven and earth, who return to Him after death in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني نميتهم ويبقى الرب جل جلاله، ونرث أهل السماء وأهل الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim is a ṣiddīq, meaning a believer in God; the same word describes Jesus' mother as a believer.
rows.anchor: إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا } ، يعني مؤمنا بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim asks his father Azar why he worships idols that cannot hear or see and cannot benefit him in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: ولا يغني عنك شيئا } [آية: 42] في الآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge that came to Ibrahim is clarification of what happens after death; he asks his father to follow his religion on a just, straight path, meaning Islam.
rows.anchor: يعني البيان، { ما لم يأتك } ، يعني ما يكون من بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan means obeying him in worship; Satan is disobedient to the Merciful and accursed.
rows.anchor: يعني لا تطع الشيطان في العبادة، { إن الشيطان كان للرحمن عصيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim fears that his father will suffer punishment in the Hereafter and become close to Satan there.
rows.anchor: يعني أن يصيبك، { عذاب من الرحمن } في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azar asks whether Ibrahim rejects his idols and threatens to stone him, meaning insult him here; elsewhere in the Qur'an the same threat means killing.
rows.anchor: يعني لئن لم تسكت لأشتمنك، { واهجرني مليا } [آية: 46]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maliyyan means for the length of Azar's life or, alternatively, for a long time: Ibrahim must leave and prolong the separation.
rows.anchor: يعني أيام حياتك، ويقال: طويلا، واعتزلني وأطل هجراني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains Azar's instruction as leaving him unharmed, without suffering injury from him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: واعتزلنى سالم العرض لا يصيبك منى معرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim answers with peace and promises to ask his Lord to forgive his father, since God has been gracious and gentle toward him.
rows.anchor: سلام عليك سأستغفر لك ربي إنه كان بي حفيا } [آية: 47]، يعني لطيفا رحيما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim separates from his family and their idols, leaving Kutha for the Holy Land; he will pray for his father's forgiveness, hoping not to be disappointed.
rows.anchor: فكان اعتزاله إياهم أنه فارقهم من كوثا، فهاجر منها إلى الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Ibrahim left his people and their idols and migrated to the Holy Land, God granted him Isaac and Jacob; Ibrahim, Isaac, and Jacob were all prophets.
rows.anchor: بعد الهجرة إلى الأرض المقدسة، { إسحاق ويعقوب وكلا جعلنا نبيا } [آية: 49]، يعني إبراهيم، وإسحاق، ويعقوب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy means His blessing; the three were given lasting, elevated good mention, praised by adherents of all religions after them.
rows.anchor: يعني ثناء حسنا رفيقا يثني عليهم جميع أهل الأديان بعدهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was a sincere Muslim who affirmed God's oneness, and was a Messenger and prophet.
rows.anchor: يعني مسلما موحدا، { وكان رسولا نبيا } [آية: 51]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God called Moses on Friday night from the mountain and brought him near for private speech; an unseen veil separated them, and Moses heard the pen's scratching.
rows.anchor: يعني دعوناه ليلة الجمعة، { من جانب الطور الأيمن } ، يعني من ناحية الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The private conversation was behind an unseen veil, and Moses heard the pen's sound or scratching.
rows.anchor: وكان بينهما حجاب خفي سمع صرير القلم، ويقال: صريف القلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granted Aaron to Moses as a prophet in response to Moses' requests for Aaron as his minister and for him to be sent to help.
rows.anchor: فأرسل إلى هارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael was Abraham's own son and a Messenger and prophet; he kept his promise to a man by waiting three days until the man returned.
rows.anchor: إسماعيل } بن إبراهيم لصلبه، { إنه كان صادق الوعد } ، وذلك أن إسماعيل، عليه السلام، وعد رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael's family means his people; he commanded them to pray and give alms, and was approved by his Lord.
rows.anchor: يعني قومك، { بالصلاة } ، وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: وكان يأمر قومه بالصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masud has 'his people' where the verse has 'his family.'
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: وكان يأمر قومه بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris was Noah's grandfather, named Akhnukh, and was a believer in God's oneness and a prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو جد أبي نوح، واسمه: أخنوخ، عليه السلام، { إنه كان صديقا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised Idris to the fourth heaven, where he died, when he prayed for the angel who directs the sun.
rows.anchor: يعني في السماء الرابعة، وفيها مات، وذلك حين دعا للملك الذي يسوق الشمس.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets include Idris from Adam's descendants; Ibrahim from those carried with Noah; Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob from Ibrahim; and Moses and Aaron from Israel, who is Jacob.
rows.anchor: ثم إدريس، { وممن حملنا مع نوح } في السفينة، يقول: ومن ذرية من حملنا مع نوح في السفينة، وهو إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the prophets to Islam and selected them for the prophetic mission; on hearing the Qur'an, they prostrated and wept.
rows.anchor: يعني إذا قرىء عليهم كلام الرحمن، يعني القرآن، { خروا سجدا } على وجوههم، { وبكيا } [آية: 58]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, believers among the People of the Torah; their prostration and tears are paralleled in al-Israʾ.
rows.anchor: نزلت في مؤمني أهل التوراة عبد الله بن سلام وأصحابه، نظيرها في بني إسرائيل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bad successors after the prophets are the Jews; this warns Muhammad's community not to imitate their bad succession.
rows.anchor: يعني من بعد النبيين خلف السوء، يعني اليهود، فهذا مثل ضربه الله عز وجل لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neglected prayer by delaying it past its appointed times and followed desires, including permitting marriage to a paternal half-sister's daughter; elsewhere following desires is glossed as fornication.
rows.anchor: يعني أخروها عن مواقيتها، { واتبعوا الشهوات } ، يعني الذين استحلوا تزويج بنت الأخت من الأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayy is a valley in Hell that the successors will encounter in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة، وهو واد في جهنم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repent from idolatry, believe Muhammad and God's oneness, and do good will enter Paradise; none of their good deeds will be reduced in recompense.
rows.anchor: من الشرك، { وآمن } بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، يعني وصدق بتوحيد الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gardens of Eden were promised by the messengers in worldly life to believing servants who had not seen them; the promise will arrive and cannot fail.
rows.anchor: المؤمنين على ألسنة الرسل في الدنيا، { بالغيب } ولم يروه، { إنه كان وعده مأتيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, laghw means swearing oaths while drinking wine; instead, angels greet the people with peace, and fruit arrives morning and evening in the manner of worldly daybreak and dusk.
rows.anchor: يعني الحلف إذا شربوا الخمر، يعني لا يحلفون كما يحلف أهل الدنيا إذا شربوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salam is the angels' greeting to the people of Paradise, and their provision is fruit timed to the two ends of the day in this world.
rows.anchor: يعني سلام الملائكة عليهم فيها، { ولهم رزقهم فيها بكرة وعشيا } [آية: 62]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God bequeaths Paradise to the servants who are sincere toward Him.
rows.anchor: من عبادنا من كان تقيا } [آية: 63]، يعني مخلصا لله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet for forty days, or, in another account, three days; Meccan polytheists said his Lord had abandoned and hated him. When Gabriel came, each expressed longing for the other.
rows.anchor: أن جبريل، عليه السلام، احتبس على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أربعين يوما، ويقال: ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel descends only by God's command; God's authority covers the Hereafter, the world, and what lies between them, including the interval between the two blasts. This answers the claim that God forgot the Prophet.
rows.anchor: { له ما بين أيدينا } من أمر الآخرة، { وما خلفنا } من أمر الدنيا، { وما بين ذلك } ، يعني ما بين الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of the heavens, earth, and all creatures is to be worshipped as one; the Prophet should patiently persist without haste. God has no namesake among the deities, since He prevents people from calling another god Allah.
rows.anchor: يقول: واصبر على توحيد الله عز وجل ولا تعجل حتى يأتيك أمري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who denies being raised alive after death is Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi.
rows.anchor: وهو أبي بن خلف الجمحي: { أإذا ما مت لسوف أخرج حيا } [آية: 66] من الأرض بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God admonishes people to reflect that He created them the first time from nothing.
rows.anchor: يقول: أولا يتذكر الإنسان في خلق نفسه، { أنا خلقناه } أول مرة، يعني أول خلق خلقناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears to gather the disbelievers with the devils who misled them and bring them all to Hell, kneeling.
rows.anchor: يعني لنجمعنهم { والشياطين } معهم الذين أضلوهم في الآخرة، { ثم لنحضرنهم حول جهنم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From each religious faction God will begin by extracting its most rebellious leaders in disbelief to punish them in the Fire.
rows.anchor: يقول: لنخرجن، ثم نبدأ بهم من كل ملة، { أيهم أشد على الرحمن عتيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best which people are most deserving of burning in Hell: the leaders in disbelief.
rows.anchor: يعني من هو أولى بها، يعني القادة في الكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person, righteous or wicked, will enter Hell.
rows.anchor: يعني وما منكم أحد إلا داخلها، يعني جهنم، البر والفاجر.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When Nafi ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about entering Hell, Ibn Abbas said that both he and Nafi would enter and challenged him to see whether they would emerge.
rows.anchor: عن نافع بن الأزرق، أنه سأل ابن عباس عن الورود، فقال: يا نافع، أما أنا وأنت، فندخلها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says that all four Qur'anic uses of wurūd mean entering: here, Pharaoh leading his people into the Fire, the idolaters' entry, and the gods' failure to escape it.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال: للورود في القرآن أربعة مواضع، يعني به الدخول

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God makes the Fire cool and safe for believers as He did for Abraham; this decree is written in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: قال: قضاء واجبا قد قضاه في اللوح المحفوظ أنه كائن لا بد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescues those who feared idolatry, the people of monotheism, from Hell and leaves the polytheists kneeling there.
rows.anchor: الشرك منها، يعني أهل التوحيد، فنخرجهم منها، { ونذر الظالمين } ، يعني المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the clear Qur'an is recited, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn ʿAlqama and other disbelievers boast to believers, wearing fine clothes with oiled hair, and ask which group has better status and housing in Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن، { بينات } ، يعني واضحات، { قال الذين كفروا } ، وهم النضر بن الحارث بن علقمة وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maqāman means a place to live, as in 'a noble residence'; nadiyyan means an assembly, as in the verse about wrongdoing in one's gathering.
rows.anchor: يعني أفضل مقاما للمساكن من مساكن مكة، ومثله في حم الدخان:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qarn is a nation; God destroyed earlier nations with softer furnishings and a better appearance than Mecca's people, destroying their wealth and bodies.
rows.anchor: قبل أهل مكة، { من قرن } ، يعني أمة، كقوله عز وجل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' question about which group has better status is answered: those persisting in idolatry may be extended provision until they see either the worldly punishment at Badr or the Resurrection, when they will know they have the worse abode and fewer followers than the believers.
rows.anchor: يعني من هو في الشرك، { فليمدد له الرحمن مدا } ، في الخير؛ لقولهم للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment may be worldly killing at Badr or the Resurrection; the disbelievers will then know their worse place and smaller faction.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا، يعني القتل ببدر، { وإما الساعة } ، يعني القيامة، { فسيعلمون من هو شر مكانا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the believers' guidance by increasing their faith; the lasting good works are four phrases of glorification, praise, monotheism, and magnification, whose reward and return are better than the disbelievers' Hell.
rows.anchor: من الضلالة، يعني يزيدهم إيمانا، { والباقيات الصالحات } ، وهي أربعة كلمات: سبحان الله، والحمد لله، ولا إله إلا الله، والله أكبر
